First, let's recall the following result:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}z=\operatorname{arctan}⁡(z)+C
$$

We proceed by setting the lower bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to -\infty .$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{-1}\frac{8}{1+{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}z & =8\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }{\int }_{a}^{-1}\frac{1}{1+{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}z \\  & =8\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }[\operatorname{arctan}⁡(z)]_{a}^{-1} \\  & =8\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }[\operatorname{arctan}⁡(-1)-\operatorname{arctan}⁡(a)] \\  & =8\cdot (-\frac{\pi }{4}-{lim}_{a\to -\infty }[\operatorname{arctan}⁡(a)])\end{aligned}
$$

Now, recall the end behavior of the function $y=\operatorname{arctan}⁡x,$ shown in the graph below:

- ${lim}_{x\to -\infty }[\operatorname{arctan}⁡x]=-\frac{\pi }{2}$

- ${lim}_{x\to \infty }[\operatorname{arctan}⁡x]=\frac{\pi }{2}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14039465/assets/27ec65761e5119be666e69b67b2fa2fcb7b4f3665ddc41faddd6c136d5c955b1.png)

Using this to evaluate our integral, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{-1}\frac{8}{1+{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}z & =8\cdot (-\frac{\pi }{4}-{lim}_{a\to -\infty }[\operatorname{arctan}⁡(a)]) \\  & =8\cdot (-\frac{\pi }{4}-(-\frac{\pi }{2})) \\  & =8\cdot (\frac{\pi }{2}-\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =2\pi .\end{aligned}
$$
